subject: Surge Health enablement — streaming + tool-call + structured output handoff
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@surgehealth.com>

Date: 2028-09-03T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Surge Health enablement — streaming + tool-call + structured output handoff

Hi Aisha,

Congrats again on the contract — excited to get Surge Health live. This thread will be our handoff from pre-sales to the enablement/implementation squad. I want to align on the minimum plan to unblock engineering and product for a pilot that exercises streaming + function/tool calling + structured JSON outputs.

Proposed Sprint0 goals (2 weeks):
- Streaming ingest + prefix/KV caching smoke test
- One function/tool integration (DocuSign signing flow) via tool-call
- JSON schema for the primary output (order confirmation object) with validation and regression hooks

Can you confirm stakeholders and availability for a 60-minute implementation kickoff this week? If helpful, I attached the initial schema draft and a short mutual action plan (MAP) with owners.

Attachments: surge_stream_schema_v1.json (schema draft), Surge_Enablement_MAP_Sprint0.pdf (action plan)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internal resources once we lock the time.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Aisha Malik <aisha@surgehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.r@surgehealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-03T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge Health enablement — streaming + tool-call + structured output handoff

Thanks Jonas — excited to kick this off.

Attendees:
- Aisha Malik (Product Lead)
- Diego Ramos (Platform Engineer)
- Lina Chen (Security, will join if we reach the security checklist items)

A few clarifying Qs before the kickoff:
1) For the DocuSign flow, we currently have an internal middleware that proxies outbound requests — can Redwood's tool-call call our internal webhook, or does it require direct external service config?
2) What are the latency SLOs we should expect during the pilot for streaming responses (p95 token latency)?
3) We saw the schema draft — can you confirm whether Redwood plans to enforce schema validation server-side or provide a client-side linting tool only?

We can do a kickoff on Thursday 09/06 at 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Malik
Product Lead, Surge Health
aisha@surgehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@surgehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-04T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge Health enablement — streaming + tool-call + structured output handoff

Great — Thursday 09/06 10:00 PT is confirmed on our side (calendar invite to follow). Quick answers so Diego and Lina can prep: 

1) Tool-call destinations: Redwood supports both direct external service integrations and customer-hosted webhooks inside your VPC (Private mode). For the pilot we can proxy to your middleware if you expose a stable HTTPS endpoint; we’ll also run a short connectivity test during kickoff. Monica will own the tool-call contract.

2) Pilot latency SLOs: our baseline for comparable configs is p95 token latency <= 250ms under light load (no batch). We’ll provide a profiling report after Sprint0 with expected variance depending on model and sequence length.

3) Schema validation: we provide both. Server-side validation is available as an optional enforcement policy on routes (reject responses that don’t match schema). We also ship a CLI lint that teams can run locally during CI. For a pilot we typically start with linting + alerts, not hard rejects.

I’m attaching the MAP with assigned owners and a slightly updated schema notes doc. Monica — can you post a short technical checklist we should run during the kickoff (connectivity, auth, sample payloads)?

Thanks,
—Jonas


From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@surgehealth.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.r@surgehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-05T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge Health enablement — streaming + tool-call + structured output handoff

Hi all — Monica from Implementation here. Short checklist for Thursday's kickoff (I kept it pragmatic):

Pre-kickoff asks (please have these available):
- A short tokenized sample payload we can use for streaming (max 512 tokens)
- A stable HTTPS endpoint + example request/response if you want Redwood to call your middleware (include auth header format)
- A sample JSON instance for the order confirmation object you want validated

Kickoff agenda (60m):
- 00-10m: Introductions & success criteria alignment (Jonas/Aisha)
- 10-25m: Connectivity & auth verification (Diego + Redwood infra)
- 25-40m: Tool-call wiring demo (DocuSign proxy scenario)
- 40-50m: Schema walk-through & validation modes (server-side vs lint)
- 50-60m: Next steps, owners, and sprint0 timeline

Implementation notes / gotchas:
- Streaming: we'll enable prefix KV caching by default in the pilot; if you have long-lived contexts ( >2k tokens) tell us so we can tune eviction.
- Tool-calls: Redwood signs outbound calls with a short-lived cert token; if your middleware expects a static API key we can map that via a vault entry during Sprint0.
- Schema: we prefer JSON Schema Draft 7 for backward compatibility; we can convert OpenAPI response schemas if that helps.

Attachments: none in this message — earlier schema and MAP are attached in the thread root.

See you Thursday.
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Aisha Malik <aisha@surgehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-09-08T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge Health enablement — streaming + tool-call + structured output handoff

Thanks — this looks good. Diego will bring the sample payloads and the middleware endpoint (we'll share the staging endpoint and a temporary API key in the kickoff). Lina is on standby for the security checklist.

Confirmed for 09/06 10:00 PT — we actually prefer 09/08 10:00 PT due to scheduling (apologies for the flip); can you update the invite? If 09/08 works for your team, we can have the following acceptance criteria for Sprint0:
- Successful end-to-end streaming sample with KV cache warmed (<= 300ms p95)
- One functioning tool-call to our staging middleware (signed request + response)
- Schema linting integrated into our CI with one validation test passing

If you can confirm the new date/time and the acceptance criteria, we'll treat the MAP as binding for Sprint0 and start internal prep.

Best,
Aisha
